title: Release train contingency lanes and calendar harmonization for runtime/console/api
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Problem: As Redwood scales simultaneous launches across runtime, console, and API surfaces we lack a compact, prescriptive playbook covering (1) blackout windows for dependent infra changes, (2) contingency lanes for automated rollback/fallback across model variants, and (3) an aligned calendar that avoids inter-team contention during high-risk time windows. Current guidance is distributed across docs and has led to two near-miss incidents in the last six months where console and runtime deploys conflicted.

Goal: Produce a single operational playbook and shared calendar controls that: (A) define dependency gating criteria and blackout windows per team, (B) create lightweight contingency lanes (auto-fallback model variant + region rollbacks) that engineering can opt into, and (C) provide a published calendar with escalation owners and automation hooks (Slack channel, status page, and a rollout dashboard). The playbook should be prescriptive enough for on-call and PMs to make go/no-go decisions and lightweight enough not to slow down PLG launches.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A published playbook page in Confluence summarizing blackout windows, dependency gates, contingency lanes, and escalation flows.
2) A shared Google calendar (team-accessible) with colored lanes for runtime/console/api and a locking mechanism for high-risk windows.
3) A minimal automation prototype: a webhook that prevents console/infra deploys during locked windows and posts an override request to a triage Slack channel.
4) Clear owner assignments for escalation and rollback with runbook links.
5) Rollout rehearsal completed with one canary + fallback test between runtime and console teams and a retro documented.
decisions: Blackout windows will be defined at 3 risk tiers (Low/Medium/High) tied to the last-mile SLO impact matrix rather than fixed time-of-day blocks.
Contingency lanes will default to model-variant fallback plus regional traffic shift; full database schema rollbacks are out of scope for this initiative.
Locking automation will be implemented as a lightweight webhook that can be added to CI pipelines; manual overrides must require two approvers (one PM, one Eng lead).
next_steps: Align with runtime, console, and API leads on risk tier thresholds (meeting scheduled 2026-02-18).
Draft Confluence playbook skeleton and share with on-call rotation for feedback (Due 2026-02-22).
Eng teams to scope webhook integration points and rough ETA for prototype (ENG owners: ENG-5821, report back 2026-02-28).
Create shared calendar and seed Q2 windows based on current release plans (PM to publish 2026-03-01).
